cards.title: Fixed Prepositional Patterns
rule: Definition: Fixed Prepositional Patterns (ቋሚ መስተዋድዳዊ ቅርጽታት) are abstract syntactic collocations where specific verbs, adjectives, or nouns must strictly be paired with designated prepositions. These combinations are idiomatic and cannot be determined through literal translation.

In English, prepositions are not always used to express literal relationships of space or time. Instead, they often function as bound lexical partners to specific words ($$\text{Word} + \text{Preposition}$$). Unlike English, Tigrinya utilizes a small, generalized set of clitic prepositions prefixed directly to nouns (e.g., "ብ-" [by/with/for], "ን-" [to/for], "ኣብ" [in/on/at], "ናብ" [to/towards]). Because a single Tigrinya prefix corresponds to multiple English prepositions, Tigrinya speakers consistently experience negative language transfer (ኣሉታዊ ምስግጋር ቋንቋ) when attempting to translate prepositions literally. This systematic grammatical divergence is heavily exploited by exam writers in high-stakes national examinations.

Adjective-preposition collocations represent a highly tested category. Key patterns include *interested in* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{in}$$), *good/bad/clever at* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{at}$$), *afraid of* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{of}$$), and *proud of* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{of}$$). A classic matriculation trap arises with the adjective *good* when describing skill or proficiency. In Tigrinya, one uses the locative prefix "ኣብ" (in/at), saying "ንሱ ኣብ ሒሳብ ጎበዝ እዩ" (literally: in mathematics he is skilled). Direct L1 transfer leads students to write or select the incorrect English forms $$\times \text{good in mathematics}$$ or $$\times \text{clever in English}$$. In standard English, the only correct collocation is *good at* ($$\text{good} + \text{at} + \text{Noun/Gerund}$$).

body: Definition: Fixed Prepositional Patterns (ቋሚ መስተዋድዳዊ ቅርጽታት) are abstract syntactic collocations where specific verbs, adjectives, or nouns must strictly be paired with designated prepositions. These combinations are idiomatic and cannot be determined through literal translation.

In English, prepositions are not always used to express literal relationships of space or time. Instead, they often function as bound lexical partners to specific words ($$\text{Word} + \text{Preposition}$$). Unlike English, Tigrinya utilizes a small, generalized set of clitic prepositions prefixed directly to nouns (e.g., "ብ-" [by/with/for], "ን-" [to/for], "ኣብ" [in/on/at], "ናብ" [to/towards]). Because a single Tigrinya prefix corresponds to multiple English prepositions, Tigrinya speakers consistently experience negative language transfer (ኣሉታዊ ምስግጋር ቋንቋ) when attempting to translate prepositions literally. This systematic grammatical divergence is heavily exploited by exam writers in high-stakes national examinations.

Adjective-preposition collocations represent a highly tested category. Key patterns include *interested in* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{in}$$), *good/bad/clever at* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{at}$$), *afraid of* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{of}$$), and *proud of* ($$\text{Adjective} + \text{of}$$). A classic matriculation trap arises with the adjective *good* when describing skill or proficiency. In Tigrinya, one uses the locative prefix "ኣብ" (in/at), saying "ንሱ ኣብ ሒሳብ ጎበዝ እዩ" (literally: in mathematics he is skilled). Direct L1 transfer leads students to write or select the incorrect English forms $$\times \text{good in mathematics}$$ or $$\times \text{clever in English}$$. In standard English, the only correct collocation is *good at* ($$\text{good} + \text{at} + \text{Noun/Gerund}$$).

Verb-preposition patterns also contain significant transfer traps. Key collocations include *congratulate on* ($$\text{Verb} + \text{on}$$), *accuse of* ($$\text{Verb} + \text{of}$$), *depend on* ($$\text{Verb} + \text{on}$$), and *suffer from* ($$\text{Verb} + \text{from}$$). Tigrinya speakers routinely write the incorrect $$\times \text{congratulate you for passing}$$ because they translate "ብምሓለፍካ" (for/by your passing) as "for". The correct English pattern is strictly *congratulate someone on something* ($$\text{congratulate} + \text{Object} + \text{on} + \text{Noun/Gerund}$$). Similarly, *accuse* must be paired with *of* (e.g., *accuse of theft*), whereas translating literally from Tigrinya "ብምስራቕ ተኸሲሱ" often results in the incorrect use of *with* or *by*.

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: The school principal warmly congratulated the top-performing students ________ achieving straight A's on the ESSLCE.

steps.text: The verb 'congratulate' requires the preposition 'on' followed by a noun or gerund: $$\text{congratulate} + \text{someone} + \text{on} + \text{something}$$.
Students often choose 'for' (Option A) because they translate 'ብምሓለፍካ' (for your passing) directly into English.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The school principal warmly congratulated the top-performing students ________ achieving straight A's on the ESSLCE.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The verb 'congratulate' requires the preposition 'on' followed by a noun or gerund: $$\text{congratulate} + \text{someone} + \text{on} + \text{something}$$.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'for' (Option A) because they translate 'ብምሓለፍካ' (for your passing) directly into English. This is a classic negative L1 transfer trap on national examinations. Option B is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Congratulate' (እንኳዕ ሓጎሰካ ምባል) ዝብል ግሲ ወግዒ ወትሩ ምስ 'on' ዝብል መስተዋድድ ጥራይ እዩ ዝስዕብ (congratulate on - Option B)። ተማሃሮ 'ብምሓለፍካ' ንምባል 'for' (Option A) ብምጥቃም ክጋገዩ ይረኣዩ እዮም፤ እዚ ግን ዓቢ ናይ ምስግጋር ቋንቋ ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Aster has always been exceptionally clever ________ mathematics and chemistry, which is why she wants to study engineering.

steps.text: Adjectives describing skill or proficiency (like *good, bad, clever, expert*) must strictly be paired with the preposition 'at' ($$\text{clever} + \text{at} + \text{subject}$$).
Students often choose 'in' (Option A) because they translate the Tigrinya locative prefix 'ኣብ' (in math) directly into English.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Aster has always been exceptionally clever ________ mathematics and chemistry, which is why she wants to study engineering.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
Adjectives describing skill or proficiency (like *good, bad, clever, expert*) must strictly be paired with the preposition 'at' ($$\text{clever} + \text{at} + \text{subject}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'in' (Option A) because they translate the Tigrinya locative prefix 'ኣብ' (in math) directly into English. Option B 'at' is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ናይ ክእለትን በላሕነትን መግለጺታት (good, clever, bad) ወትሩ ምስ 'at' ዝብል መስተዋድድ ጥራይ እዮም ዝስዕቡ (clever at - Option B)። ተማሃሮ ነቲ 'ኣብ ሒሳብ ጎበዝ እዩ' ዝብል ናይ ትግርኛ መዋቕር ብምቕዳሕ 'clever in' ክብሉ ይጋገዩ እዮም።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: The regional government is trying to find a viable solution ________ the severe water shortage in our town.

steps.text: Nouns representing entries, answers, or solutions (like *solution, key, answer, response*) strictly require the preposition 'to' ($$\text{solution} + \text{to} + \text{noun}$$).
Students often choose 'of' (Option A) because they translate possessive phrases like 'ናይዚ ጸገም መፍትሕ' (the key of this problem) directly, resulting in the incorrect use of 'of'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The regional government is trying to find a viable solution ________ the severe water shortage in our town.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
Nouns representing entries, answers, or solutions (like *solution, key, answer, response*) strictly require the preposition 'to' ($$\text{solution} + \text{to} + \text{noun}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'of' (Option A) because they translate possessive phrases like 'ናይዚ ጸገም መፍትሕ' (the key of this problem) directly, resulting in the incorrect use of 'of'. Option B is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Solution' (መፍትሒ) ዝብል ስም ወትሩ ድሕሪኡ 'to' ዝብል መስተዋድድ እዩ ዝወስድ (solution to the problem - Option B)። 'of' ምጥቃም ናይ ትግርኛ 'ናይ...' ዝብል መዋቕር ቀጥታዊ ትርጉም ስለ ዝኾነ ሰዋስዋዊ ጌጋ ይፈጥር።

questions.q: The school principal warmly congratulated the top-performing students ________ achieving straight A's on the ESSLCE.
questions.label: 1. The school principal warmly congratulated the top-performing
why: The verb 'congratulate' requires the preposition 'on' followed by a noun or gerund: $$\text{congratulate} + \text{someone} + \text{on} + \text{something}$$.
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: Aster has always been exceptionally clever ________ mathematics and chemistry, which is why she wants to study engineering.
questions.label: 2. Aster has always been exceptionally clever ________ mathemat
why: Adjectives describing skill or proficiency (like *good, bad, clever, expert*) must strictly be paired with the preposition 'at' ($$\text{clever} + \text{at} + \text{subject}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The regional government is trying to find a viable solution ________ the severe water shortage in our town.
questions.label: 3. The regional government is trying to find a viable solution
why: Nouns representing entries, answers, or solutions (like *solution, key, answer, response*) strictly require the preposition 'to' ($$\text{solution} + \text{to} + \text{noun}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The local community is highly proud ________ the young students who won the national science fair award.
questions.label: 4. The local community is highly proud ________ the young stude
why: The adjective 'proud' must strictly be paired with the preposition 'of' ($$\text{proud} + \text{of} + \text{noun}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The suspect was accused ________ stealing valuable medical equipment from the regional public hospital.
questions.label: 5. The suspect was accused ________ stealing valuable medical e
why: The passive verb 'accused' must strictly be paired with the preposition 'of' ($$\text{accused} + \text{of} + \text{noun/gerund}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The delayed arrival of the school bus is typical ________ the local transport system during the rainy season.
questions.label: 6. The delayed arrival of the school bus is typical ________ th
why: The adjective 'typical' (meaning characteristic of) must strictly be paired with the preposition 'of' ($$\text{typical} + \text{of} + \text{noun}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: Your academic success in university will heavily depend ________ how hard you study now.
questions.label: 7. Your academic success in university will heavily depend ____
why: The verb 'depend' strictly requires the preposition 'on' ($$\text{depend} + \text{on} + \text{noun/clause}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The violent storm caused severe damage ________ the historic school building last night.
questions.label: 8. The violent storm caused severe damage ________ the historic
why: The noun 'damage' (when referring to harm done to something) must strictly be paired with the preposition 'to' ($$\text{damage} + \text{to} + \text{noun}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: When I was a young boy living in the village, I was extremely afraid ________ wild dogs.
questions.label: 9. When I was a young boy living in the village, I was extremel
why: The adjective 'afraid' must strictly be paired with the preposition 'of' ($$\text{afraid} + \text{of} + \text{noun}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The principal was very angry ________ the students who cheated during the chemistry test.
questions.label: 10. The principal was very angry ________ the students who cheat
why: When 'angry' modifies a personal object (someone), it must strictly be paired with the preposition 'with' ($$\text{angry} + \text{with} + \text{person}$$).
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q: The man was _______ of stealing the car.
why:
In English, certain verbs are paired with specific prepositions. The verb **'accused'** is followed by the preposition **'of'** (accused of something). 

*   **'Charged'** is followed by **'with'**.
*   **'Arrested'** and **'blamed'** are followed by **'for'**.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: The community is very proud ____ its athletes.
questions.label: 12. The community is very proud ____ its athletes.
questions.tip: Learn adjective + preposition and verb + preposition pairs as fixed chunks: proud of, interested in, good at, depend on, congratulate on, apologise for.

questions.q: The principal congratulated the students ____ their results.
questions.label: 13. The principal congratulated the students ____ their results.
why: The fixed pattern is "congratulate someone on something".
So: congratulated the students on their results.
questions.tip: Learn adjective + preposition and verb + preposition pairs as fixed chunks: proud of, interested in, good at, depend on, congratulate on, apologise for.

questions.q: The success of the project depends ____ teamwork.
questions.label: 14. The success of the project depends ____ teamwork.
why: "depend of" is a common L1 error.
questions.tip: Learn adjective + preposition and verb + preposition pairs as fixed chunks: proud of, interested in, good at, depend on, congratulate on, apologise for.

questions.q: Correct the error: "She is married with a doctor."
questions.label: 15. Correct the error: "She is married with a doctor."

similar.q: Correct: He is interested on science.

questions.answer: She is married to a doctor.
why: The fixed pattern is "married to someone".
"married with" is incorrect in standard English.
questions.tip: Learn adjective + preposition and verb + preposition pairs as fixed chunks: proud of, interested in, good at, depend on, congratulate on, apologise for.

questions.q: Aster is clever ____ mathematics.
questions.label: 16. Aster is clever ____ mathematics.
why: Ability adjectives (good, clever, bad, excellent) take "at".
questions.tip: Learn adjective + preposition and verb + preposition pairs as fixed chunks: proud of, interested in, good at, depend on, congratulate on, apologise for.

questions.q: The government is looking for a solution ____ the water shortage.
questions.label: 17. The government is looking for a solution ____ the water shortage.

similar.q: Complete: What is the answer ____ question 5?
Complete: There is no cure ____ this disease yet.

why: The fixed pattern is "a solution to a problem".
So: a solution to the water shortage.
Similar: the answer to, the key to.
questions.tip: Learn adjective + preposition and verb + preposition pairs as fixed chunks: proud of, interested in, good at, depend on, congratulate on, apologise for.

questions.q: Read: "The students were worried about the exam, but the teacher reminded them of their hard work and encouraged them to believe in themselves." Which phrase contains the fixed pattern "verb + of"?
questions.label: 18. Read: "The students were worried about the exam, but the teacher reminded them of their hard work…

similar.q: Complete: She was worried ____ her brother.

why: "remind someone of something" is the fixed pattern with "of".
"worried about" and "believe in" use other prepositions.
"encouraged them to" is verb + object + infinitive.
questions.tip: Learn adjective + preposition and verb + preposition pairs as fixed chunks: proud of, interested in, good at, depend on, congratulate on, apologise for.

questions.q: He insisted ____ paying for the meal.
questions.label: 19. He insisted ____ paying for the meal.
why: The fixed pattern is "insist on + -ing / noun".
questions.tip: Learn adjective + preposition and verb + preposition pairs as fixed chunks: proud of, interested in, good at, depend on, congratulate on, apologise for.

questions.q: True or false: "different from" is accepted in formal English.
questions.label: 20. True or false: "different from" is accepted in formal English.

similar.q: Complete: This book is similar ____ that one.
Complete: Your answer is different ____ mine.

why: True. "different from" is the standard formal pattern.
("different than" and "different to" exist in some varieties but are less safe in exams.)
